notes.title: Make Your Kingdom is OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[b]Make Your Kingdom[/b] is now available for everyone here on Steam! 🎉 And for those who are new to the game let us introduce it to you.

[b]Make Your Kingdom[/b] is a city-building game where you have to build, expand and improve your settlement. Become a leader of a brand new kingdom, keep your people happy and the economy thriving, fight orcs and have fun!

The game few features unique to its genre, such as:

[list]
[*] Play as a founder of the settlement - you can help build your kingdom, carry the resources, talk to other settlers and motivate them, fight off hordes of orcs with your own sword!
[*] Choose between a few different looks of various buildings - customize your settlement the way you want!
[*] No stress sandbox mode - create without any limitations! In this mode, your settlers can’t starve, get sick or die. Fires, weather conditions, earthquakes, and orcs can no longer destroy your buildings.
[*] The changing of the seasons - each season brings its own challenge, but all are equally beautiful.
[/list]
We can't wait to read all your comments and reviews and let's hope that the game runs smoothly for all of you! Soon we'll be posting a guide here for everyone that wants to have a bit more insight on the game but so far we'll let you dive in and explore on your own ;) Cheers! 🥂

notes.title: Orcs in Make Your Kingdom: Warriors, Arsonists, and Thieves
notes.notes:
Hello Founders! 

Today we are going to tell you about the varieties of orcs in Make Your Kingdom. You remember that orcs in Make Your Kingdom are dead settlers who have been resurrected and are out for blood. Even the clothes on the orcs are the same as on the former humans. 

Some of them are particularly dangerous, while others are terribly annoying. But all must be wary and fight them with all their might to save the still-living inhabitants of your kingdom.
Orcs of War (Warriors)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/9c4f3dad63515d20e8424388a067667d8c87e83f.png[/img]
The name speaks for itself - these orcs live for battles. Each one is armed with huge axes and loves to fight. These guys are the most dangerous of all, so watch out, train your army and equip it! Especially with bows and armor.
Arsonists
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/a7db99b6c35dcda45c255442c5729cd5d8ed0a25.png[/img]
Orcs with torches whose main goal is to burn your kingdom to the ground. Destroy them or you lose all the buildings. As soon as the arsonist completes his task and uses the torch, he will turn into a thief.

Thieves
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/82463f44aa2188a5c7aedce0b968440a057925d9.png[/img]
The most annoying kind of orcs! Thieves steal your resources and damage buildings, and then flee into the woods. There are a lot of them, they run fast and are terribly annoying. 

***

That's all! Don't forget to join our Discord, where we give away a copy of MYK once a week in a contest, and have also scheduled a Q&A session: https://discord.gg/YPz9P9QA

notes.title: Devlog #6: the world of the game and useful tips
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello, founders![/h2]

Today we're going to talk about Make Your Kingdom literally: the size of the map, its properties, and where best to place your settlement so that it can become a kingdom after all! 
[h2]Big World[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/189003d3aeaead8b38388fa4b62334e9bdbd3b83.jpg[/img]
Size matters in Make Your Kingdom! The full version of the game will have the option to start the game on one of three maps. The maps are generated differently every new game:

A small map - suitable for beginner founders who are just getting acquainted with the game and settlement management. The size of this map is 350 squares x 350 squares (1 house occupies 2 squares).
The middle map is 475 x 475 squares. Since it is larger than the previous map, it has a larger spread of resources.
The large map is 600 x 600 squares. A map for advanced founders! Resources are scattered randomly over a huge space. But the bigger the map, the bigger the kingdom!
[h2]Diverse World [/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/0916d9bb292b38d8034459a020722dc407f34d1d.gif[/img]
The world in Make Your Kingdom is really diverse - sometimes the same locations can be drastically different from their previous versions. 

The game will have different seasons with different properties (we talked about them in one of the previous development diaries). For example, in winter the settlers freeze.
Many landscape variations: mountains, fields, ponds, lakes, forests, brushwood. Remember that you can only build on flat surfaces! And try to build your settlement near mountains and forests to be close to resources.
[h2]One Chance at the Start [/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/e4446d3b7cf1deb17f27bbe1479284c465f42406.gif[/img]
At the beginning of each game you will only get one chance to choose the starting location of your settlement. You can only build one main building, which means there will only be one settlement on the large map! 

But you will be able to build other buildings in different parts of the map. The only problem will be that if you choose a bad location at the start, the resource sources will be far away and the settlers will have to run far away. This means that resources will be slow to replenish!

***
That’s all!

notes.title: Housing problem in Make Your Kingdom
notes.notes:
Hello Founders! Today we're going to talk about renovating houses in Make Your Kingdom. Does that sound boring? See what you have to say after the first earthquake or the invasion of orcs rising from the dead. 
[h2]Housing Question[/h2]
Make Your Kingdom is the nicest construction and settlement management simulation, but even here things can happen that are not nice at all. For example, earthquakes can destroy parts of a settlement, as can orcs during raids. And even the passage of time gradually destroys buildings! 

See how scary and at the same time beautiful the doomed settlement looks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/7ce5e0b6f602dfca73366c1e043fac09695b16b8.gif[/img]

If you lose all of your vital buildings, your settlers will die and the game will be over. You can't let that happen!
[h2]Repair time [/h2]

And how to keep the settlement in a more or less acceptable form for life? Or put it in order after a disaster? Let's look into it.

The services of an architect. Yes, there is an architect in your kingdom. From time to time he has to inspect buildings and fix them up. Would you like to do everything yourself? You can do that too! Switch to single settler control mode and fix the buildings yourself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/f34809825becc26977be3713102bf93be8028e6b.gif[/img]

Damaged buildings can catch fire. In this case, you will have to put them out first and only then repair them. If you don't make repairs in time, the building will explode! Destroyed buildings cannot be rebuilt, only rebuilt. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/0fc6d10426a1efcb6c40a76d456c3fe63687c822.gif[/img]

Everything is interconnected! Even if just one building is destroyed, the chain of production may be disrupted. For example, if there is no Farm, the Sheep Farm, where you can get meat and wool, cannot function. Without these resources you won't be able to feed your settlers and make weapons and armor for them. 

Buildings are repaired with planks. So don't forget to resupply to keep your settlement looking good. 

That's all for now, Founders! 

By the way, Make Your Kingdom is just over a month away from release. To celebrate, we're holding weekly giveaways in our Discord, with the grand prize being a Make Your Kingdom Steam key! Join in and take part: https://discord.gg/73v3KVtW

notes.title: Protecting the settlement and fighting the Necro-orcs in Make Your Kingdom
notes.notes:
Hello, Founders! In this Make Your Kingdom devlog, we're going to talk about how to protect your settlement and fight off Necro Orc raids. Get your low-poly weapons ready and pay attention, because this devlog will save your settlers! 

[h3]The end is only the beginning[/h3]

Sometimes the sweet world of Make Your Kingdom can be harsh. For example, if you don't build enough huts, your settlers may freeze outside in the winter. Lack of food is also an important problem. Disease and starvation are unfortunately followed by death.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/db5e67ae5445ce96f1e4cfa6409b3fec37a2826b.jpg[/img]

However, death in Make Your Kingdom is just the beginning. After death, the settlers become... no, not zombies, but orcs! It's an unexpected twist, isn't it? Turning into mad monsters, they attack everyone around them, even their former neighbors. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/76f01e74643b2f2038269584172a4f090e7ba235.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/84944e959d4ce6c9dc8c80d20496cefac4428b1c.png[/img]

[h3]Protection against necro-orcs[/h3]

A shield, bow and sword are the best tools for defending against orcs in Make Your Kingdom. Produce iron, create weapons, and arm your guards with them if you want to save your settlement! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/5bc8e0463e35e24e8cac7a4a0eff5e6a8336f8a6.jpg[/img]

Your settlers will fight on their own. But if you have a warrior's spirit, you can switch to a third-person view and personally lead your soldiers into battle! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/396c390213d261711879939dd000e9b809566835.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/2cf6eacf2d09c1c347037bb429de53c719ad0b81.gif[/img]

However, fighting is a last resort. To defend the settlement, you can build walls and towers with archers and guardsmen. They will either delay the onslaught of undead orcs, or even help repel it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/01cfd1496611134c9bdd69f2c2bef12b2b02a18e.gif[/img]

notes.title: Useful Resources and Survival Ways in Make Your Kingdom
notes.notes:
Hello Founders! Today we're going to talk about the resources with which you can build a successful settlement and how to acquire them! Sit back on your throne as this tutorial will help you become a successful Founder!

[h1]Fresh low-poly food [/h1]

In Make Your Kingdom, in order to feed all of your settlers, you need to get food. There are several kinds of food.

[list]
[*] Meat is obtained from sheep farms. The meat itself is inedible, so you have to make nice low-poly sausages from it at the Butcher's House. The meat makes the settlers work faster, as do the buildings where the meat-eaters are located.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/6b0855f975ae3f08fdb7e97eba2ddce1eb870928.png[/img]

[list]
[*] Wheat is also an important resource for sustenance. In a mill wheat becomes edible bread. 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/bc256a5acca1b16816eafb4fad645901cd6b6483.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] Wild berries and fruits - they can be collected from bushes and trees. Green berries can be used to make medicine in the Healer's House. Fruits are used to make cider, which will come in handy in the tavern to keep your settlers in good spirits! 
[/list]

[h1]Resources for luxury low-poly apartments[/h1]


In addition to edible resources, Make Your Kingdom also has resources that can be used to build houses, defenses, and even flying machines! 
[list][*] At the sheep farm you can get wool - it can be used to make cloth, and you need it for the blimps that bring in new residents for your settlement and for your archers to defend themselves against orc raids! [/list]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/dad0bb805d467c95332410aa43a86f0692b4d009.png[/img]

[list]
[*] Wood is extracted by lumbermen and foresters in the forest. The logs in the forester's house are used to make boards, which are needed for construction and charcoal.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/70473a73a9a2849ae757affc6bc8ed998afad1ba.png[/img]

notes.title: Developer Diary 1 (Part 2)
notes.notes:
[i]Yo_serjio is an indie game developer working on low-poly city building game with survival elements called «Make Your Kingdom». Right now you can already try a [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1257560/Make_Your_Kingdom_Prologue/]free demo[/url] of the game and leave your opinion on it.
Despite its simple and cute visuals the game can get quite hardcore and challenging - try to fight back an orc pack, survive the harsh winter or manage the needs of your people without letting the settlement get completely destroyed.
[/i]

[b]Developer Diary 1 (Part 2)[/b]


[b]Home, sweet home[/b]
 

When you develop a city builder you have to think up all kinds of different resources. The materials for the construction and food for people gotta come from somewhere. I decided to keep the resource system pretty classic. You have wood, stone, berries. meat, wool, coal, wheat, fabric etc. Production of some of the resources depends on having the other resources. For example, you can’t get coal without wood or fabric without wool, which seems pretty logical.
 
The game has different types of building and structures. The system is pretty standard too: the main building, a basic house, an architect house, a butcher’s house,  a textile factory, a coal burner, a forester’s house, etc.
 
Here is an important thing: the more satisfied your people with the living conditions, the more places you have for them in the house. These conditions include: having food, water, coal, etc. It depends on the house’s surroundings - if you don’t have a well near the house, there won’t be any water. A residential building can also get a second floor if a lot of people are happy with their life there. The player can choose which buildings to destroy, but don’t get too carried away with it if you don’t want to set your whole city on fire. ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37137594/f798fbf55da1c521f161386bd450f921893be255.png[/img]
 

[b]In the beginning was…[/b]
 

Make Your Kingdom: Prologue, which is an alpha demo of the game, has recently been released, and as you could notice, it has some bugs, restrictions and a lot of experimental stuff. But, I mean, what else did you expect from an alpha demo? :) 
 
You can test all the basic mechanics in the demo: play as a head of the city and see the life of your people up close, fight orcs, try to survive the harsh winter, build all the different structures (there will be a lot more buildings in the full game though) and unlock some achievements!
 
Putting the free demo out on Steam was a really important step and a right one too. It let me see the game through the players’ eyes. You also helped me test the existing game mechanics, discover a lot of bugs and issues and all the reviews you left has already put an impact on the development of the full game.
 
The idea of releasing a prologue came to me because I always want to try out the certain game myself before actually buying it. But not every game these days has a demo. Or the demo just lets you play through the small section of the already finished game. I find this kinda boring. MYK Prologue is a different story - it’s a place for us all to experiment and I’m glad that so many people decided to be a part of it.
 
[b]Per aspera ad astra[/b]
 

Even though Make Your Kingdom has been in development for several years already, I know that there is still a lot to do. The prologue already showed me all the things that needs to be changed or added. 
 
Actually, I was really eager to see your feedback. Some may say that if there is no criticism or suggestions then everything about your game is perfect. But that’s not true. There is always room for improvement. If people don’t critique your game and leave no suggestions or questions, it means that barely anyone cares about your project. And when you put your heart, soul and time into something, lack of people’s interest in it is literally the worst.
 
When you develop a game by yourself, you just can’t find all the bugs or test every mechanic properly or optimize it to be playable on every PC. That’s why you need actual players trying it out.
 
So if you like games and especially good games, try to leave your feedback every now and then, it really helps the devs out. But try to keep it constructive too. Sure, you can take your frustration out in the comments or in the review without letting the developer know about the actual issues with the game, but is it really gonna help anyone? I don’t think so. That’s why I hope that you’re giving me constructive criticism and feedback. :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37137594/7e6288bef596d1223c4cc3f263228dcd848a181b.png[/img]
 

[b]Something ends, something begins[/b]
 

And finally I want to thank all of you for reading the first diary, I hope it was somewhat entertaining. And if you’d like to see more of these - let me know. I hope you are having fun playing the demo and don’t forget to follow Make Your Kingdom on social media if you want to see exclusive content that’s not on Steam. ;) As they say, «Keep calm and stay tuned». Bye everyone! :)
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37137594/1e481d244242707d70d4977ee36037f5ce9b607c.png[/img]

notes.title: Developer Diary 1 (Part 1)
notes.notes:
[i]Yo_serjio is an indie game developer working on low-poly city building game with survival elements called «Make Your Kingdom». Right now you can already try a [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1257560/Make_Your_Kingdom_Prologue/]free demo[/url] of the game and leave your opinion on it.
Despite its simple and cute visuals the game can get quite hardcore and challenging - try to fight back an orc pack, survive the harsh winter or manage the needs of your people without letting the settlement get completely destroyed.
[/i]

[b]Developer Diary 1 (Part 1)[/b]
 
Hello, my name is Sergey Yurkin (or you may know me as yo_serjio) and I’m the main and only developer of «Make Your Kingdom» - a low-poly city building game where you have to build, expand and improve your settlement. Developing a game is a difficult process but when you have to do every bit of work by yourself it becomes a real trial. I've been working on «Make Your Kingdom» for more than two years and I'm basically used to this trial by now, but let’s start from the beginning.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/6b2aecb6aa7ad138cdc441d543b83a6d1e13854f.png[/img]
 
[b]How I decided to make my own kingdom[/b]
 
When I was a child I liked playing economic simulation games and city building games. I could play them all day and night really. My personal favorites were «Simcity», «Knight and Merchants», «The Settlers 2», «Pharaoh» and «Caesar». All these games have left an imprint on me and I still feel inspired by them. I liked building cities and their infrastructure, monitor the needs and the mood of the settlers and just watching them live their lives. All these aspects that I enjoyed so much as a child I tried to replicate in «Make Your Kingdom». Maybe some of the old school gamers will even feel nostalgic playing my game, at least I hope so! But the game has a lot to offer for all the new school gamers too.

Before this project I was working on the other game that I was building with MonoGame. Then one of my friends suggested to check out Unity. And since the programming language was basically the same I decided to give Unity a try. I really enjoyed working in it and got inspired to make a brand new project.

When it came to choosing the visual style of the game I tried many different effects and shaders until I found the combination of the ones that I personally found most fitting.

The main effects that create and atmosphere in the game are: volumetric light, hard shadows from light sources and the refraction of light between objects. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/400111a7ea4cfc7fbde6d0f677fe493dc8672b41.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/72d6268b654df2d2964d5599e2c79b265967126e.png[/img]

I also tried various shaders for water - realistic ones and cartoony ones, but decided to go with a mix between these two styles since it fits the game style the best. 

Another influence in terms of visuals was the relatively new game «Kingdom and Castles». There was one thing about it that I didn’t like though - the vivid colours that I find too bright and unnatural. For «Make Your Kingdom» I chose more calm, pastel colors.

I like how the game looks right now and I think it already has its own unique vibe and visual aesthetic. And because of the overall simple look it’s also easily recognisable. :)

Fun fact - the first step in the development of «Make your Kingdom» was writing a script for the construction of the building - it was at the end of 2017. You can take a look at it [url=https://twitter.com/yo_serjio/status/944452154332536832]here[/url].

[b]Kingdom from the inside[/b]

Developing a game follows all the main principles of city building games - you have to go from a nondescript settlement to a huge and rich kingdom. And I’ve experienced it firsthand.

As I said earlier, I was inspired by my favorite childhood games and borrowed a few mechanics from them. For example, in «Knight and Merchants» and «The Settlers 2» I really liked the way you can track how the resources move from the moment they are made to the moment they are used or remade into another resource.

In «Pharaoh» and «Caesar» I liked the management of the city through the fulfilment of citizens' needs. All these mechanics made their way into «Make your Kingdom» in one form or another.

In addition, there are a number of mechanics that make the game unique, like being able to play as one of the settlers and see the city from the inside. This makes the player feel more immersed in the game. Playing as a settler you can help harvest food, carry the resources from one place to the other and even fight orcs!

Speaking of orcs, making sure that your people are happy and satisfied with their lives is really important. Unhappy settlers can turn into orcs and leave the city just to later attack it and take their revenge out on you for all the social injustice. 

Another potential threat is a harsh winter. In the future I’d also like to add a few natural disasters and other calamities to spice things up for the players.

All new settlers come to the city on the airship, but not all of them might stay due to the lack of housing or  other unsatisfactory conditions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/02653593e3f8d06004ccef13dc9070667d5ca0d7.png[/img]

This is the end of part one of this developer diary. I plan to release developer diaries quite regularly. Stay tuned for more if you’d like to know how «Make Your Kingdom» is being developed!

notes.title: Farm and Windmill
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/6c11e0d16e4ba39f4a9d060674d5258d3f5911c5.png[/img]
Bread is the staff of life! Your people need a Farm and a Windmill to make bread. They grow wheat on a Farm and then recycle it in the Windmill. And Bob’s your uncle!

notes.title: Charcoal Maker
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/ad1c588e5387f2beabc3628aa57f5fa5a44fd2a3.jpg[/img]
Hello! Settlers have a lot of needs and a desire to warm up in severe frosts is one of them. Build the Charcoal Maker that produces a coal and your people won’t freeze in the winter

notes.title: Stay safe and stay home!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/cc5910ac2aa387b36a58ed0c966f9148296d365c.jpg[/img]
Our settlers keep their social distance and wear face masks. Don't forget about these rules if you have to leave your kingdom!

notes.title: Market
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/3d3f6e5d8534697a431f82e863304fd2ab2c1e3a.png[/img]
If you want to meet the needs of the settlers, build the Market. There they will be able to buy whatever they want!

notes.title: Mine
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/e1f170d29f49a55d169fa3d89e42b1e26b98d93c.png[/img]

Stone is a necessary resource for building all kinds of structures. In order to acquire some stone you'd have to build a Mine. Mine can only be placed in the mountains, but be careful - building it too close to the citizens' houses might make them unhappy.

notes.title: Forestman House
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/61224279f88997f17ae58604aedc5ce706ac0f71.jpg[/img]

One of the key buildings in the game is the Forestman house, which supplies the settlement with logs and wooden boards. The Forestman himself plants the trees and chops them off, he also recycles wood. This character is a must-have for your settlement!

Are you excited to play it? What are your expectations? Share your current thoughts on the game with me! :D

notes.title: The House
notes.notes:
Every person needs a place in a House - this is one of your citizens' primary needs. If you won't be able to make sure that everyone has a place to live in, homeless citizens will turn into orcs and leave the city. Orcs in the wild is a threat to your settlement. Your buildings can also start to collapse and you'll find out how to prevent their destruction very soon!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/a89c66c1b3b901ebe6c70a36df46ef962497c147.png[/img]
Share your thoughts on this building with me! Do you like how it looks and functions? Would you change anything? I really appreciate your feedback. :)

notes.title: The Main Building
notes.notes: Hi everyone! I wanna tell you a little bit more about the buildings that the game has so far. The Main Building is the center of the city. It’s essentially a player’s residence and all the roads in the settlement lead to it. The airship brings new citizens and all kind of resources there. At the first stages of the game you can find some wooden boards and rocks there to make your initial buildings.[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/2b119ea0f3a16099f30216ea4e69037a57651761.png[/img]

notes.title: Gameplay features
notes.notes: The game takes place in a world that lives by its own laws. Sometimes nature will test your strength. Don’t forget to monitor the condition of your buildings, fire safety and others important aspects.[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33942180/f05942f5843224077cb4c0cc51cca25ba974f64a.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Difficulty level
notes.notes:
In some city building games the player has a way to choose or change the difficulty level. In MYK the game gets more difficult the further it progresses and you can't choose the level of difficulty yourself. At least that's how it is so far! What do you prefer: being able to choose the difficulty level or to follow the game algorithms?
